llm.summary: ClawLint is a local, static security linter for OpenClaw skills whose required operations and files are consistent with its stated purpose; nothing in the package asks for unrelated credentials or network installs.

dimensions.detail: The name/intent (static audit of OpenClaw skills) matches the included shell script and SKILL.md. The script scans skill directories, looks for suspicious patterns, and optionally computes SHA256 — all appropriate for a linter. Minor metadata mismatch: the registry lists no required binaries but the SKILL.md (and the script) expect standard Unix tools (sha256sum, grep, awk, stat, base64, readlink, mktemp, etc.). This is explainable but should be noted.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and the script perform static analysis only (no code execution or network calls). They scan files under configured skill roots and flag patterns (hardcoded secrets, curl|bash, sudo, etc.). The script does detect and report symlinks and will not, by default, follow them when enumerating ordinary files (it uses find -type f and separately flags -type l). It does allow scanning arbitrary directories via --root if the user supplies them, which is expected for a tool that can be pointed at different locations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided and the package is instruction-only with an included shell script. Nothing is downloaded or installed automatically; this is the lowest-risk install model and aligns with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials and does not attempt to access remote services. The only notable inconsistency is that the registry metadata reported 'no required binaries' while the SKILL.md/script require standard Unix utilities; JSON output is documented as 'requires Python 3' but the top-level need checks in the script do not enforce python presence (some JSON plumbing may exist in omitted/truncated code). No secrets or unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (default) and disable-model-invocation:false — normal for a skill. The tool does not modify other skills or system configuration; it only reads files and optionally computes hashes. It does not request permanent presence or elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: ClawLint appears to be a coherent, local static-audit tool. Before running: 1) confirm you have the required Unix tools listed in SKILL.md (sha256sum, grep, awk, stat, base64, readlink, mktemp, etc.); 2) be aware it scans the skill directories you point it at (default: ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills and ~/.openclaw/skills) and can be told to scan other roots via --root, so don’t point it at directories you don’t want read; 3) the tool flags symlinks but may still enumerate symlink files differently — review flagged symlinks so you’re not inadvertently exposing files outside the skill; 4) JSON output is documented to require Python 3 (the script’s truncated portion may rely on a Python helper), so ensure python3 is available if you need JSON; 5) the registry metadata omission of required binaries is a small inconsistency — verify the environment meets the script’s need before running. Overall: reasonable to install and run, but as with any security tool, inspect the script yourself and run it in a non-privileged environment if you have concerns.
